newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Health Council to tackle smoking, blood, communicable diseases.
newsitem.headline: Health Council to tackle smoking, blood, communicable diseases.

text.p: The Health Council, recognising that adoption of the draft directive banning tobacco advertising is still politically impossible, will try instead on Tuesday to adopt a resolution on ways to cut tobacco consumption.

The Council will also adopt texts on blood safety and diseases such as the human equivalent of mad cow disease and hold debates on legislation to create a network for monitoring communicable diseases and on the proposed European Health Card.
It will also adopt as an "A" (non-discussion) point a decision to set up a drug dependence programme.

TOBACCO. The draft tobacco resolution urges EU states to continue to promote strategies to curb smoking, noting that these include restricting access of minors to tobacco products, increasing tobacco taxes and barring smoking in public areas.

It says the Commission should examine possible further measures the EU could take to support national anti-smoking initiatives and to present reports on progress in promoting coordination between EU states.
EU officials said it was not clear the text would be adopted as a Council text since Britain and Greece, a big tobacco producer, had some objections to it.
Supporters of the long-blocked legislation to ban all tobacco advertising, COM(92)196, say the tide could turn if Britain's Labour Party wins the national election which must be called by late May.
Labour is expected to reverse Britain's opposition to the proposal, which could allow it to go through.

BLOOD SAFETY. The Council is expected to adopt a resolution asking EU governments and the Commission to take action to promote blood safety and self-sufficiency. It says the governments should review their procedures and programmes in light of recommendations outlined by a group of experts who met in Adare, Ireland, in September.

TSEs. The Council is set to adopt conclusions asking EU states to step up coordination to prevent the spread of Transmissible Spongiform Encephalopathies (TSE) -- such as mad cow disease -- among humans.

The Commission has updated a working document on the question which complains that data on Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD), the human equivalent of mad cow disease, is not uniformly monitored and evaluated by member states.
It says the EU needs common criteria for collecting, analysing and disseminating information on CJD surveillance.
COMMUNICABLE DISEASES. The Council will hold an orientation debate on a draft decision, COM(96)78, to set up an EU network for monitoring and controlling communicable diseases.

Among questions to be debated are the legal base, the obligations of member states, the Commission's role and whether the network should perform simply a monitoring function or have the power to impose controls such as quarantines, EU officials said.

Some member states vehemently object to mandatory coordination of countermeasures, so the Irish presidency has proposed a compromise calling for member states to consult when they take measures and to coordinate with their EU partners on a voluntary basis, EU officials said.
HEALTH CARD. The Council will debate the possibility of introducing a European Health Card carrying electronic information about an individual's health in case of emergency.

DRUG DEPENDENCE PROGRAMME. The Council will adopt as an "A" point a decision, COM(94)223, to spend 27 million Ecus during 1996-2000 on efforts to help member states coordinate their efforts to fight drug addiction.
